plain.li: [first] A year ago today {SUBJECT} was born here, the first child the colony ever had. {A_nameDef} was up before dawn and has looked in on the cradle three times since.
[years] {YEARS} years since {SUBJECT} was born, the first of the colony's children. {A_nameDef} still tells the story of that night, down to who boiled the water.
On this day the first child born in the {PLACE} came into the world. {A_nameDef} wants small gifts passed round, as they were the night {SUBJECT} was born.
[tradition] The first child's day has been kept so many years now that gifts start turning up by the door before breakfast. {A_nameDef} left the first of them.
[winter] {SUBJECT} was born in the cold, and the day comes round in the cold. {A_nameDef} has the fire built up early.
[devout] The day {SUBJECT} was born. {A_nameDef} gave thanks at dawn for the first child the colony was given, and asks that the gifts be blessed before they go round.

warm.li: {SUBJECT}'s day. {A_nameDef} has kept a scrap of the blanket {SUBJECT} was first wrapped in, and brought it out this morning.

gloomy.li: The day the first child was born here. {A_nameDef} remembers how thin the stores were that season, and says so to anyone at the table.

cheerful.li: {SUBJECT}'s day! {A_nameDef} has been wrapping things in cloth since before breakfast and won't let anyone see.

plain.li: [new] {SUBJECT} was born today. The first child born here, and the only one of us who won't remember living anywhere else.
[new] A child, here, ours. People came to the door one at a time to look, and most of them took their boots off first.
[!new,first] A year since {SUBJECT} was born. Gifts went round the circle again, and {SUBJECT} tried to eat one.
[!new,years] {YEARS} years since the first child was born here. One of the children asked me what the colony was like before. I didn't know where to start.
[!new,tradition] The first child's day, kept the way we always keep it: gifts round the circle and far too much fuss.

warm.li: [new] {SUBJECT} slept on my chest most of the afternoon. So small. I didn't want to move.
[!new] Carved a wooden bird for {SUBJECT}'s day and got a hug that nearly knocked me over.

blunt.li: [new] A child born here today. Healthy. Loud.
[!new] First child's day. Gave a gift, got one. Good day.

cheerful.li: [new] A baby, born here, ours! I've started on a cradle and I've never made one in my life.
[!new] {SUBJECT}'s day! I gave a whittled spoon and got a ribbon, which I'm still wearing.

gloomy.li: [new] A child born here today. I hope this place is kinder to the child than it has been to the rest of us.
[!new] {SUBJECT}'s day. I watched the children at the circle and thought about the things I can't keep from them.

cold.li: [new] First birth recorded here. That room will need a cradle, and later a second bed.
[!new] {SUBJECT}'s day again. The child is growing; we'll need more beds before long.

plain.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} remembered the night {SUBJECT} was born, and how long it went on.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} about {SUBJECT}'s first word.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} talked about how fast the colony's children are growing.
{A_nameDef} showed {B_nameDef} the gift {A_pronoun} made for the first child's day.
[first] A year ago the last stretch went up and the colony was walled in all the way round. {A_nameDef}, who built more of it than anyone, has been walking it since breakfast.
[years] {YEARS} years since the walls went up. {A_nameDef} wants a fire lit by the wall tonight, the way one was lit the night the last section went in.
The walls' day. {A_nameDef} went round them before dawn with a lantern, checking every joint, which is how the day begins now.
[tradition] The walls' day, kept so long that the wood for the fire was stacked by the gate before anyone asked. Tonight someone will tell the story of the last section again.
[tribal] The day the palisade closed. {A_nameDef} says the spirits of the place have watched over it ever since.
[medieval] The day the walls went up. {A_nameDef} has hung a garland over the gate, as the old towns did on their walls' day.
[afterraid] The walls' day, and they held again this year. {A_nameDef} says that's reason enough for the fire.

blunt.li: Walls' day. {A_nameDef} wants the fire built against the north wall, same as last time.

cold.li: The day the walls went up. {A_nameDef} says the colony has been measurably safer every day since.

gloomy.li: The walls' day. {A_nameDef} spent the morning looking for cracks, and found two.

plain.li: [new] The last section of wall went in today. I walked the whole length of it before supper, slapping it every few steps.
[new] We have walls. Real ones, all the way round. I'll sleep better tonight than I have since we came.
[!new,first] A year since the walls went up. We lit a fire and sang, and I put my hand on the wall as if it could feel it.
[!new,years] {YEARS} years behind these walls. They've earned their fire.
[!new,tradition] The walls' day, kept the old way. Someone always tells the story of the last section, and it's never quite the same story.

warm.li: [new] The walls are up. I know whose hands built which stretch, every one of them.
[!new] The walls' day. I sat with the old building crew at the fire and we named every stretch we put up.

blunt.li: [!new] Walls' day. Fire. Patched the east corner first.

cheerful.li: [new] The walls are finished! I ran all the way round them twice.
[!new] The walls' day! We danced round the fire till the sparks gave out.

gloomy.li: [new] The walls are up. Now we find out what they're for.
[!new] The walls' day. Every year I count the patched places, and every year there are more.

cold.li: [new] Perimeter complete. Our odds against the next raid are a good deal better.
[!new] The walls' day. People patched the walls before the fire without being told. Useful.

plain.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} went over which stretches of the wall each of them built.
{A_nameDef} argued with {B_nameDef} about which stretch of the wall was the hardest to build.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} that the walls have held every time it mattered.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} the story of the last section, the way it's told on the walls' day.
[first] A year ago today {SUBJECT} came home safe after {COUNT} days on the road. {A_nameDef} still remembers the first sight of the gate.
[years] {YEARS} years since {SUBJECT} came home from {COUNT} days away. {A_nameDef} wants the long table laid the way it was that night.
The homecoming. {A_nameDef} has been telling the newcomers about the road home, starting, as always, with the ford.
[tradition] The homecoming. By noon there were people at the gate for no reason but the day, and the long table is already out.
[winter] The homecoming comes round in the snow. {A_nameDef} says the road home was worse.

warm.li: The homecoming. {A_nameDef} has been telling people all morning how good it is to be home, as if the road were only yesterday.

cheerful.li: The homecoming! {A_nameDef} lit a lantern in the gate, the same one that hung there that night.

cold.li: The homecoming. {A_nameDef} notes that the journey cost no lives, which is not how most long ones end.

plain.li: [new] Home. {COUNT} days on the road and I'd forgotten what my own bed felt like.
[new] Came through the gate this afternoon and they were all there waiting. I didn't know how much I'd missed them.
[!new,first] A year since we came home. We ate at the long table and told the road stories, and they were better than the road was.
[!new,years] {YEARS} years since the homecoming. I still look at the gate at dusk, out of habit.
[!new,tradition] The homecoming, kept as always. I could tell the road stories in my sleep by now.

warm.li: [new] Home safe. Someone had kept my bed made the whole time.
[!new] The homecoming. Ate at the long table next to people who weren't even here back then.

cheerful.li: [new] Home! I kissed the gatepost. I'm not ashamed.
[!new] The homecoming! I told the story of the river crossing and it got a round of applause.

gloomy.li: [new] Home at last. Some nights out there I didn't think we'd make it.
[!new] The homecoming. I think about the ones on the road who didn't have a gate to come back to.

cold.li: [new] Returned after {COUNT} days, in one piece. A good result.
[!new] The homecoming. The ones who stayed behind like this day more than the ones who traveled.

plain.li: {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} about the road home, and the river that nearly stopped them.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} remembered the day {SUBJECT} came home.
{A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef} whether {B_pronoun} would ever go on a long journey again.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} what it was like to see the colony's smoke from the hill on the last day.
[first] A year ago the colony brought in its first {SUBJECT}. {A_nameDef}, who grew it, still keeps a pouch of seed from that first harvest.
[years] {YEARS} years since the first {SUBJECT} came in, and {A_nameDef} was walking the rows again before breakfast.
The day of the first {SUBJECT}. {A_nameDef} asked for it to go on the calendar, and has been out in the field since dawn.
[tradition] The day of the first {SUBJECT}. The colony keeps it every year now, and {A_nameDef} tells the story of the seed.
[lowtech] {A_nameDef} has hung the first {SUBJECT} of the year over the door, the way it was done the first time.

cheerful.li: The day of the first {SUBJECT}! {A_nameDef} has been showing people the field since breakfast, whether they asked or not.

cold.li: The first {SUBJECT}'s day. {A_nameDef} has worked out what the crop has saved the colony in trade since, and would like it mentioned at the feast.

plain.li: [new] Brought in the first {SUBJECT} today. New seed, strange soil, and it took. I could hardly believe it.
[new] Our first {SUBJECT}. Not much of it yet, but it's ours.
[!new,first] A year since the first {SUBJECT}. It grows like it was always meant to grow here.
[!new,years] {YEARS} years of {SUBJECT} now. I still remember the first handful.
[!new,tradition] The day of the first {SUBJECT}, kept as always. I told the story of the seed again.

warm.li: [new] The first {SUBJECT} came in today, and people kept stopping by the field to look.
[!new] The first {SUBJECT}'s day. I took some round to the ones who helped with that first field.

cheerful.li: [new] The first {SUBJECT}! I talked to those plants every morning and I'm sure it helped.
[!new] The day of the first {SUBJECT}! I wore some of it in my hair all evening.

gloomy.li: [new] The first {SUBJECT} came in. One good crop. We'll see about the next.
[!new] The first {SUBJECT}'s day. One more thing to lose to the blight.

cold.li: [new] First harvest of {SUBJECT}. One more thing we no longer have to buy.
[!new] The first {SUBJECT}'s day. A crop that has lasted this long is a crop we can count on.

plain.li: {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} how close the first {SUBJECT} came to failing.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} argued about where the {SUBJECT} seed first came from.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} that {SUBJECT} grows better in the {PLACE} than anyone expected.
[first] A year ago today the colony made its first trade. {A_nameDef} struck the deal, and has been telling people how hard {A_pronoun} bargained ever since.
[years] {YEARS} years since the first trade. {A_nameDef} wants small gifts round the circle, the way the colony shared out what came in that day.
The day of the first trade, when the colony stopped being alone in the world. {A_nameDef} has dug the first coin out of the strongbox to pass round.
[tradition] The day of the first trade, and gifts are going round the circle already.
[tribal] The day of the first trade with another people. {A_nameDef} set out the first things the colony gave and got, side by side, on a hide.

blunt.li: The day of the first trade. {A_nameDef} still says {A_pronoun} got the better of it.

cheerful.li: The day of the first trade! {A_nameDef} has a gift for everyone and won't say what any of them cost.

plain.li: [new] Struck our first trade today. I think I got the better of it.
[new] We traded with someone today. It feels like being let into the world.
[!new,first] A year since the first trade. Gifts round the circle; mine was a bone needle in a leather case.
[!new,years] {YEARS} years since we first traded. We're known on the roads now.
[!new,tradition] The day of the first trade, with gifts as always.

warm.li: [new] Our first trade. The trader shook my hand at the end, and I think meant it.
[!new] The first trade's day. I gave a small thing and got a small thing, and both were lovely.

blunt.li: [!new] Gifts for the first trade's day. Nice.

cheerful.li: [new] Our first trade, and I haggled. I'm a haggler now!
[!new] The first trade's day! I got a carved comb and I've used it four times since lunch.

gloomy.li: [new] Traded with strangers today. They know where we are now.
[!new] The first trade's day. I still wonder what they told the next village about us.

cold.li: [new] First trade concluded. A colony that trades doesn't have to make everything itself.
[!new] The first trade's day. Trade has done more for us than most of our walls.

plain.li: {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} what the colony got in its first trade, and what it gave.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} argued about who really got the better of the first trade.
{A_nameDef} gave {B_nameDef} a small gift for the day of the first trade.
[first] A year ago today the hunters brought down {COUNT} head of game in a day, mostly {SUBJECT}, and the colony ate well for a week. {A_nameDef} led them, and wants to lead them again.
[years] {YEARS} years since the great hunt. {A_nameDef} had the hunters up and fed before dawn.
The day of the great hunt. {A_nameDef} has been watching the tree line since first light.
[tradition] The great hunt, and the hunters are out before the sun is up, as every year.
[tribal] The day of the great hunt. {A_nameDef} painted the old marks on the hunters' faces at dawn.
[medieval] The day of the great hunt. The dogs and spears are ready, and {A_nameDef} has warned the cook.

blunt.li: Great hunt's day. {A_nameDef} wants the hunters out early and back with meat before dark.

cheerful.li: The great hunt! {A_nameDef} has been practicing the hunting call all morning, and the dogs have started answering.

plain.li: [new] {COUNT} head of game in one day, mostly {SUBJECT}. My arms ache from the carrying.
[new] We hunted from dawn till dusk and came back with more than we could carry.
[!new,first] A year since the great hunt. Out before dawn again, back after dark, tired and pleased.
[!new,years] {YEARS} years since the great hunt. The game is warier now, and so are we.
[!new,tradition] The great hunt's day, kept as always: the hunters out at dawn, the fire high at night.

warm.li: [new] A great hunt today, and nobody hurt. I'm grateful for that more than the meat.
[!new] The great hunt's day. I thanked the animals under my breath, the way I was taught.

blunt.li: [new] Big hunt. Lots of meat. Good day.

cheerful.li: [new] The best hunt we've ever had! I'll be telling this one for years.
[!new] The great hunt! My shot was the best one, whatever anyone says.

gloomy.li: [new] A great hunt, they're calling it. The forest was very still afterwards.
[!new] The great hunt's day. There's less game every year.

cold.li: [new] {COUNT} animals taken in one day. The larder is secure for some time.
[!new] The great hunt's day. Good practice for the hunters, and meat for everyone.

plain.li: {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} how the great hunt went, every shot of it.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} argued about who brought down the first of the {SUBJECT} on the day of the great hunt.
{A_nameDef} showed {B_nameDef} how to move through the brush without a sound.
{NAME}, and {A_nameDef} has been stacking wood since noon for the fire tonight.
[first] This is the first year {NAME} comes round. {A_nameDef} wants a bonfire for it, with music.
[years] {NAME} again, {YEARS} years on. The fire goes up at dusk, as every year.
[tradition] {NAME}. The wood was stacked by noon without anyone being asked.
[winter] {NAME} in the cold. A fire tonight will be welcome for more than one reason.
[named] {NAME}, a day the colony named for itself, and tonight it gets a fire.

cheerful.li: {NAME}! {A_nameDef} has found a drum somewhere and is threatening to play it all night.

gloomy.li: {NAME}. {A_nameDef} says it will rain on the fire, as it does most years, and has stacked the wood under cover anyway.

plain.li: We kept {NAME} with a fire. I sat close enough to scorch my boots and didn't move.
[first] The first time we kept {NAME}: a fire, music, sparks going up. I think it'll stick.
[years] {NAME} again. Same fire, same songs, a year older.
[tradition] {NAME}. The same songs round the fire, and I still don't know the second verse of any of them.

warm.li: {NAME}. Everyone round the fire, faces lit up orange. I looked at each of them and was glad.

cheerful.li: {NAME}! I danced till the fire was embers and then a bit more.

gloomy.li: {NAME}. I watched the sparks go up and thought about everyone who used to sit round fires with me.

cold.li: {NAME}. A fire costs some wood and buys a good deal of goodwill. Worth it.

plain.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} sat at the fire for {NAME} and talked until it burned down.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} a story at the fire on {NAME}.
{A_nameDef} taught {B_nameDef} the song the colony sings round the fire on {NAME}.
{NAME}, and {A_nameDef} has been making something in secret all week.
[first] {NAME}, the first time it's kept, and {A_nameDef} suggests gifts round the circle.
[years] {NAME} again, {YEARS} years on. Everyone has something small hidden in a pocket.
[tradition] {NAME}. People have been whittling and sewing behind closed doors for days.
[lowtech] {NAME}. {A_nameDef} has carved little gifts from offcuts, one for each of them.

warm.li: {NAME}. {A_nameDef} has been asking round, carefully, what people have been missing.

blunt.li: {NAME}. Gifts. {A_nameDef} asks that nobody give {A_objective} socks again.

plain.li: Gifts for {NAME}. I got a carved button and gave a pair of socks. A fair trade.
[first] First time we kept {NAME} with gifts. Nothing much, all of it lovely.
[tradition] {NAME}, with gifts as always. I've been planning mine since last year.

warm.li: {NAME}. The gift I got was something I'd only mentioned once, months ago. Someone was listening.

blunt.li: {NAME}. Gave a knife. Got a scarf. Fine.

cheerful.li: Gifts for {NAME}! I wrapped mine in three layers of cloth just to make it last.

gloomy.li: {NAME}. I never know what to give. I gave it anyway, and it seemed to be enough.

cold.li: {NAME}. A small exchange of gifts does more for a colony's peace than most rules.

plain.li: {A_nameDef} gave {B_nameDef} a small gift for {NAME}.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} compared what they got for {NAME}.
{A_nameDef} thanked {B_nameDef} for {B_possessive} gift on {NAME}.
{NAME}, kept with a hunt. {A_nameDef} has the hunters ready, and the pot is waiting.
[first] A new day on the calendar, {NAME}, and {A_nameDef} says the right way to keep it is a hunt.
[years] {NAME} again: the hunters out at dawn, the pot on by dusk.
[tradition] {NAME}. The hunters are already out; it's how the day has always begun.
[tribal] {NAME}. {A_nameDef} says a day worth keeping is a day worth hunting for.

cheerful.li: {NAME}! {A_nameDef} is out at the tree line already, waving the others on.

plain.li: Kept {NAME} with a hunt. Out all day, back with game.
[first] Our first hunt for {NAME}. Muddy, tired, well fed.
[tradition] {NAME}: the hunt, as always. My legs know the way now.

warm.li: {NAME}. Hunted with the others all day, and we ate what we brought home together.

cheerful.li: {NAME}! I nearly got a deer. Nearly counts on a feast day.

gloomy.li: {NAME}. A long cold day in the brush for not much.

cold.li: {NAME}. A hunt keeps the hunters sharp and the larder full. A sensible way to mark a day.

plain.li: {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} about the hunt for {NAME}, and the one that got away.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} argued about who had the better shot on {NAME}.
{A_nameDef} showed {B_nameDef} the tracks {A_pronoun} followed on {NAME}.
[way:bonfire] {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} {A_pronoun} has been stacking wood for the fire tomorrow.
[way:gifts] {A_nameDef} tried to find out what {B_nameDef} was giving tomorrow.
[way:hunt] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} looked over their weapons for tomorrow's hunt.
[kind:firstchild] {A_nameDef} reminded {B_nameDef} that tomorrow is the day the first child was born here.
[kind:walls] {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} that tomorrow it'll be another year since the walls went up.
[kind:homecoming] {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} that tomorrow is the homecoming, and started on the road story early.
[kind:newcrop] {A_nameDef} reminded {B_nameDef} that tomorrow is {NAME}.
[kind:greathunt] {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} to be up before dawn tomorrow, for the great hunt.
